subject: Isolated fleet options: private control plane vs reserved pools for Stella Health
messages:
From: Mike Rutledge <mike.rutledge@stellahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-30T16:14:00Z
Subject: Initial ask: isolated inference setup and sizing

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal and compliance teams are clear that any production inference for PHI needs to be logically isolated and auditable. We are evaluating two pathways: a private deployment in our VPC (customer-managed control plane) versus Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with network isolation and contract controls).

High level constraints:
- P95 latency target: 250ms for text generation requests (average prompt length ~120 tokens)
- Peak concurrent users: 1,600 end users via API, estimated 120 qps at business hours burst
- Long tail: occasional 30-second batch jobs for nightly bulk processing (non-interactive)
- Data residency: US only, SOC2 + HIPAA posture required

Can you sketch a sizing and cost delta for Private vs Dedicated and call out the differences in operational responsibilities and SLA implications? Also flag any gating items for a SOC2/HIPAA assessment (key management, audit logs, egress controls).

Appreciate a draft by EOD Thursday if possible.

Mike
Mike Rutledge
CTO, Stella Health
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Rutledge <mike.rutledge@stellahealth.com>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: isolated inference setup and sizing

Mike,

Thanks for the clear constraints. Attached is a draft sizing spreadsheet and a short writeup that compares the two build paths. Summary up front:

- Recommended short-term: Redwood Dedicated reserved pools using A100 80GB (quantized runtime) with strict VNet peering and egress rules. This meets latency and throughput targets with lower up-front ops overhead and faster time-to-production.
- Recommended long-term (if Stella requires full control plane): Private deployment in your VPC with dedicated H100 80GB nodes for peak windows. Higher capex and longer lead time but gives you full control over audit logs, KMS, and network topology.

Sizing numbers (draft):
- Dedicated path: 8 x A100 80GB per reserved pool (pods sized for 60 concurrent small chat sessions each), plus 2x warm spare nodes for failover. Estimated steady-state token throughput meets 120 qps with P95 ~180-220ms given our batching and KV cache.
- Private path: 6 x H100 80GB primary + 3 x H100 warm spares to meet the same SLAs; higher throughput translates to ability to consolidate some batch jobs, but requires more infra work to optimize scheduler and kernel selection.

Cost and timeline delta:
- Dedicated: 6 week procurement to reservation active, lower monthly committed cost, Redwood manages runtime and patches.
- Private: 10-14 weeks for on-prem/VPC configuration, KMS integration, and compliance attestation work. Higher initial platform fee plus recurring support contract.

Gating items for compliance:
- KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys (both supported; Private gives you direct KMS control)
- Audit logs retention policy (we can push logs to your Cloud Storage for Private; for Dedicated we provide an alternatives export pipeline)
- Data-at-rest encryption of model caches and disk volumes (both supported; note quantized artifacts may still be considered sensitive)
- Network egress allowlist and private peering (required in both configurations)

I included a conservative capacity cushion in the spreadsheet. Camila, can you confirm the kernel/quantization assumptions and whether H100 would materially reduce node count if we use 4-bit VH quantization for the model family they plan to serve?

Attached: stella-sizing-draft.xlsx, private-vs-dedicated-cost-model.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Mike Rutledge <mike.rutledge@stellahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: isolated inference setup and sizing

Mike, Jonas,

Quick technical clarifications from infra/serving:
- The A100 80GB baseline we sized assumes 8-bit or 4-bit quantized model runtime with our KV cache enabled. For many customer workloads this gets to the 180-220ms P95 we quoted. If Stella wants unquantized FP16 paths for strict quality, expect 1.4x-1.8x more GPU cycles per token.
- H100 brings better tensor core throughput and can reduce node count by 25-35% for the same latency curve, but at a higher unit cost. For the Private path we recommended 6 primary +3 spares; if they accept 4-bit quantization we could get by with 5 primary +2 spares.
- Nightly batch jobs should be scheduled on a separate batch pool to avoid affecting interactive latency. We recommend burstable credits on Dedicated or a separate fenced batch queue in Private.

Compliance notes:
- For SOC2/HIPAA, we need to validate log forwarding and retention. Private lets you control retention directly; Dedicated requires an export contract to ship logs to your storage with guaranteed retention windows.
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys is available both ways; Private has fewer handshake steps during attestation.

I'll update the workbook assumptions tab to show both quantization scenarios and the spare margin.

Camila Reyes
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
